newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says 96/97 intvn grain stocks may top 10 mln T.
newsitem.headline: EU says 96/97 intvn grain stocks may top 10 mln T.

text.p: European Union grain intervention stocks are likely to rise to more than 10 million tonnes by the end of 1996/97 (July/June), Commission officials said on Monday.
Intervention stocks stood at 2.8 million tonnes at the end of 1995/96, after falling from 9.2 million at the end of 1994/95.
"Intervention is likely to be at least 10 million tonnes," said one official, warning it was impossible to make an accurate forecast as the situation was constantly changing.

The EU farmers' lobby expects grain intervention stocks to rised to 20 million tonnes by the end of the season while the U.K.'s Home Grown Cereals Authority earlier this month forecast stocks rising to nearly 15 million tonnes.
Earlier this month at an EU cereals advisory committee meeting, Commission officials estimated that there would be 66 to 67 million tonnes of grain available for export and storage in 1996/97.
The estimate was based on production of 202 million tonnes, total supplies (including imports and stocks carried forward from last season) of 232 million and internal consumption of 165-166 million.

But since then export demand has revived because of Iraq's return to the market, India's need for large quantities of wheat and further Saudi demand for barley. Disruption of the Argentine harvest due to rain has also made prices firmer.
As a result, expectations that the EU would only export around 25-26 million tonnes of grain now appear to be pessimistic.
"Exports are now likely to be higher," said a Commission official, adding shipments could reach 30 million or even 32 million tonnes.
"Exports have been much stronger in recent weeks. If we can continue at this rate intervention would be less...but this is pure speculation," said the official.
Under the GATT world trade agreement, the EU may subsidise the export of 32.3 million tonnes of grain in 1996/97
Last season subsidised exports totalled 18 million tonnes.
